name: MERIDIAN PROSTHETICS CruxGrip Modular Hand
description:
The CruxGrip replaces the hand at the wrist joint with a full prosthetic unit driven by tendon-cable actuators and a wrist-mounted microprocessor that reads residual EMG signals from the forearm to interpret intended grip patterns. Its defining feature is the QuickLock fingertip system — each of the five fingers terminates in a standardized bayonet socket, allowing specialized fingertip modules to be swapped in under thirty seconds without tools. Modules include fine-manipulation needlepoints for surgery or electronics work, padded grip tips for delicate object handling, conductive tips for direct interface, and hardened ceramic tips for abrasive environments.

The CruxGrip is Meridian Prosthetics' flagship hand unit — affordable enough for Tier 2 hospital coverage, reliable enough that it's been the default amputation prosthetic in the Great Lakes region for eleven years. It lacks the aesthetic refinement of CHROMEWORKS or CRUCIBLE hands, with its visible cable routing and matte grey polymer casing, but its modular tip system has spawned a massive aftermarket ecosystem of third-party fingertip modules. Street vendors sell bootleg tips ranging from lockpick arrays to micro-torch fingertips.
installation_requirements: Wrist-level amputation or existing wrist disarticulation; 2-hour fitting surgery; EMG calibration session required post-op
rejection_risk: Low — polymer socket with silicone interface liner; EMG electrodes are transcutaneous
maintenance: Cable tension adjustment every 6 months; tip socket cleaning weekly; EMG electrode pad replacement annually

cultural_context: The CruxGrip's aftermarket tip ecosystem has become a cultural phenomenon on the Shelf. Tip-swap meets happen in parking structures and back-alley workshops where modders trade and sell custom fingertip modules. The line between tool and weapon blurs quickly — Meridian's official tip catalog runs to fourteen models, but the grey-market catalog numbers in the hundreds.
